identity.name: Northline Repair
identity.descriptor: Outdoor clothing and equipment repair workshop
identity.origin: The fictional northern city of Calder
identity.nameMeaning: Northline is the route where weather, use and repair become visible rather than hidden.

essence.oneLine: Northline Repair keeps trusted outdoor gear in use through visible, documented repairs.
essence.promise: You see the repair, its limits, its material and the test it passed before the item comes back.
essence.tension: Field abrasion and fluorescent workshop marks meet a disciplined technical grid.

worldview.belief: Wear is information. A good repair respects how an object is used instead of pretending damage never happened.
worldview.future: Repair history becomes a normal part of owning equipment, and products are judged partly by how well they can be maintained.
worldview.humanRole: Repair technicians inspect damage, choose a method and explain when replacement is safer.
worldview.technologyRole: Technology records materials, repair history and tests; it does not overrule physical inspection.
politicalOrSocialBoundaries: Do not turn the brand into a party-political position.
Do not use anxiety, shame or social status as sales pressure.
Do not romanticise labour or hide who performs it.

purpose.why: Useful equipment should not become waste because one component failed.
purpose.mission: Inspect, repair and document outdoor gear with methods matched to its real use.
purpose.vision: Repairability becomes a visible product quality rather than an afterthought.

positioning.category: Outdoor clothing and soft-equipment repair service
positioning.audience: People who use outdoor gear regularly, rental teams and small expedition operators
positioning.need: A trustworthy decision on what can be repaired, how it will perform and when replacement is the safer choice.
positioning.difference: Every job receives a visible repair map, material note and test result instead of a vague 'fixed' label.
proof: Each fictional repair record names method, material and test.
The fictional intake flow separates cosmetic, functional and safety-critical damage.
positioning.pricePosition: Priced by inspection, repair class and testing rather than the retail value of the item.

offers.name: Bench repair
offers.job: Restore a worn zip, seam, panel or fastening where a defined repair is appropriate.
offers.outcome: The item returns with a repair map, visible limits and completed test.
proof: Fictional repair record and test label.
notFor: damage that cannot be made safe

offers.name: Fleet record
offers.job: Track repeat repairs across rental or field equipment.
offers.outcome: A team sees failure patterns and replacement decisions by item.
proof: Fictional item history and reason codes.

audiences.name: Regular gear owner
audiences.context: A trusted jacket or pack has a specific failure but the rest still works.
audiences.job: Know whether repair is sensible and what will remain visible.
audiences.desiredShift: From 'replace it just in case' to an informed repair or replacement decision.
audiences.language: Name the part, damage, method and limit.

audiences.name: Rental or field-equipment lead
audiences.context: Many numbered items return with different patterns of wear.
audiences.job: Keep a consistent repair history and retire unsafe gear promptly.
barriers: pressure to keep everything in service
audiences.desiredShift: From scattered notes to a visible decision trail.
audiences.language: Operational, countable and explicit about uncertainty.

values.name: Inspect before promise
values.meaning: The material and use case decide what is possible.
antiBehaviours: quote certainty from a blurry image

values.name: Repair stays visible
values.meaning: A repair can look deliberate without pretending to be factory-new.

values.name: Retire responsibly
values.meaning: Keeping gear moving never overrides a safety boundary.
antiBehaviours: turn safety into a marketing claim

messaging.masterMessage: Show us the failure. We will show you the repair, the test and the limit.

messagePillars.name: Visible inspection
messagePillars.claim: Damage is classified before a repair is offered.

messagePillars.name: Known limit
messagePillars.claim: A no-repair decision is a valid outcome.

messaging.storyPattern: Begin with the worn part. Classify the failure. Show method and test. End with repair, limit or retirement.

dimensions.instruction: Name what was inspected and what remains unknown.
Use outdoor context only to explain use, not to create hero drama.
Be respectful and short; never soften a safety limit.

avoid: claims with no physical or recorded proof

do: give an owner and next update
say what happened and what remains safe
avoid: jokes during loss or payment issues

language.defaultRegister: Plain international English with precise material and component terms.
language.sentenceRhythm: Short diagnostic statements followed by one explanatory sentence. Use verbs and measured conditions.

terminology.safe: passed the stated test, never safe without scope
terminology.sustainable: state the measured material or life-extension fact

formatting: lists only when they improve scanning
language.inclusiveLanguage: Name real roles and actions. Do not invent personal characteristics or reduce an audience to a demographic stereotype.

allowed: This fictional job passed the test named on its repair record.
This fictional repair remains intentionally visible.
Northline Repair may decline work outside its fictional scope.
forbidden: a certification that does not exist
disclaimers: This is a fictional Brand DNA dataset. No company, product, customer or performance claim is real.

onBrand: Zip failure, not jacket failure. Inspection class B. Photos first.
The patch will show. So will the stitch line and the test it passed.
This webbing should be retired, not repaired. Here is why.
offBrand: Adventure further with our game-changing repair solutions.
We make every item as good as new.

concept.direction: Charcoal technical sheets, repair-tape yellow, ice blue and exposed stitch paths over field-worn material.
concept.rationale: The system treats every artifact like a repair record: damage, intervention and test remain visible at the same time.
concept.visualTension: Rough worn surfaces and exact vector annotation; cold field light and warm repair-bench focus.

usage: Yellow marks intervention, never general decoration.
Rust means unresolved or worn, never automatic failure.

gradients.name: Inspection sweep
gradients.job: Short scanning transitions in diagnostic media

rules: Set measurements and codes in mono.

logo.idea: A north-pointing route line interrupted and rejoined by a visible bar-tack stitch.

variants.background: light or dark according to the approved master

logo.clearspace: At least the cap height of the first letter on every side.
placement: align to the primary content grid
keep away from photography focal points
use one-colour variants when contrast is uncertain
dont: use the symbol as a decorative texture

layout.principle: A layered inspection sheet: object, damage, intervention and decision each have a stable lane.
layout.grid: Twelve columns on desktop, six on tablet and one stacked inspection lane on mobile.
layout.density: Dense where records need comparison, open around decisions and safety limits.
composition: annotate beside damage, never over it
keep the repair path in one accent
make before and after use identical crops
responsive: keep the primary action above bottom navigation
allow text to wrap without collision
prove zero horizontal overflow at 390 px

shapes.geometry: Route lines, stitch bars, measurement ticks and clipped label corners.
shapes.corners: 0-2 px; clipped 6 px corners may mark inspection cards.
shapes.strokes: 1.5 px records, 2 px icons, 3 px repair paths.

iconography.job: Identify damage class, repair method, test and item status at a glance.
iconography.metaphor: Components and workshop actions drawn like field-manual symbols.
iconography.grid: 24 × 24 px with a 2 px optical safe area.
iconography.corners: Mostly square; small optical relief inside tight joints.
iconography.detail: One primary form and no more than one supporting detail; test at 16 px.
iconography.color: One colour by default; repair-tape yellow marks only an active or selected state.
opticalRules: open narrow gaps at small sizes
align repeated elements to whole pixels where possible
dont: put the icon in a presentation mockup

illustration.job: Explain the relationship between material layers, damage and repair method.
illustration.style: Exploded technical sections with one fluorescent intervention layer.
illustration.perspective: Flat orthographic view; no decorative pseudo-3D.
dont: cute characters without a narrative job

photography.job: Let a viewer inspect damage, material and repair quality before reading the caption.
photography.moment: The exact point where damage is classified, stitched, sealed or tested.
composition: hands enter only when doing work
scale reference without fake ruler text
photography.camera: Stable camera at object or shoulder height; tripod for comparison records.
photography.lens: 50-90 mm with low distortion; enough depth of field to read the failure.
photography.light: Large neutral inspection source plus warm task light when stitching; no dramatic rim light.
photography.palette: Charcoal bench, actual material colours, yellow intervention markers and cool inspection light.
photography.grade: Neutral material colour, restrained contrast and recoverable highlights.
photography.texture: Abrasion, sealant, thread, weave and tool marks stay sharp and honest.
do: grade a series as one shoot

motion.principle: Motion traces inspection and intervention in the order a technician performs them.
signature: a route line stopping at damage and continuing after repair
a before/after crop locking into place
a status plate changing only after test
motion.reducedMotion: Replace spatial movement and looping signals with an immediate static state change.
avoid: motion that competes with the task

dataVisualization.principle: A repair record must distinguish observation, action, test and decision without relying on colour.
dataVisualization.colors: Chalk and charcoal as base, ice for observation, yellow for action, rust for unresolved review.
rules: never use colour as the only distinction

representation.principle: Show technicians and owners as practical decision-makers; outdoor identity comes from use and objects, not heroic demographics.

casting.people: One technician or owner at a real task; groups only for a fleet handoff.
casting.age: Adults whose age fits the real role; keep a series varied without signalling authority by age.
casting.gender: Do not assign technical skill or outdoor experience by gender.
casting.ethnicity: Choose deliberately across a series without inferring from customer or staff data.
casting.ability: Show adaptable benches and realistic handling where relevant, without using access as campaign decoration.
casting.roles: Hands belong to the person performing or receiving the repair.
casting.wardrobe: Plain work layers, repair apron and used outdoor clothing; no expedition costume.
casting.behaviour: Inspecting, measuring, sewing, testing and explaining; direct attention to the item.

representation.sensitiveAttributePolicy: Never infer ethnicity, religion, health, sexual orientation, gender identity or another sensitive attribute from a name, face, place or industry. Unknown remains unknown.
representation.consent: Recognisable real people require documented permission for the exact channel and context. Do not reuse customer or staff imagery as generic campaign material.
avoid: roles assigned through gender or age stereotypes
synthetic faces presented as real staff
children without a necessary context and explicit guardian consent

sensory.sonicIdentity: Measured workshop mechanics: thread, zip, snap and test tone with field air kept at the edge.

music.harmony: spare and slightly tense until the test resolves

voiceover.voice: Steady adult voice with clear technical diction.
voiceover.delivery: Diagnostic, calm and honest about limits.

soundEffects.role: Confirm real material actions and status.

sensory.silence: Use silence before a no-repair decision and after the named test result.

universal: Keep verified facts, fictional demonstration content, creative decisions and inference visibly separate.

repair-tape yellow must have a functional or narrative job.

Show people as capable participants, not decoration.

accessibility.standard: WCAG 2.2 AA for digital work; accessible PDF practices for documents.
contrast: Normal text must reach at least 4.5:1.
Large text and interface boundaries must reach at least 3:1.
Colour can never be the only carrier of state.
Use only pairings that have been measured, not guessed from appearance.
motion: Do not autoplay essential information without controls.
Every animated state needs an immediate static equivalent.
text: Keep body copy as selectable, scalable text.
Write links that describe their destination.
Explain specialist terms at first use.
media: Alt text describes the image's communication job.
Decorative images receive empty alt text.
Video includes captions and a transcript.

trademarks: The name is fictional but still requires a real clearance search before commercial adoption.
Never recreate a third-party mark in generated assets.
assets: Record the source and licence for every font, image, icon and sound.
Keep logo masters as vectors outside image-generation prompts.
Do not copy imagery from an unrelated real organisation into this example.
claims: Every public claim needs a real source or owner approval.
Fictional proof cannot be reused as a real testimonial.
Measure environmental, time and performance claims before stating them.
privacy: Do not add personal data that is unnecessary for the artifact.
Use recognisable people only with documented rights.
